title: Persistent Cough
differential: Lung metastasis from unknown primary source
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with persistent cough >3 weeks, hemoptysis, weight loss, chest pain, dyspnea, and fatigue. History of smoking (most common risk factor). CXR shows a solitary pulmonary nodule or mass — may have spiculated borders, pleural effusion, hilar lymphadenopathy. CT chest with IV contrast for characterization. Tissue diagnosis: bronchoscopy with biopsy, CT-guided needle biopsy, or surgical biopsy. NSCLC (adenocarcinoma most common in non-smokers, also squamous, large cell) vs SCLC (almost exclusively smokers, aggressive, central). NSCLC staging: PET/CT, brain MRI. Treatment: NSCLC stage I-II: surgical resection (lobectomy). Stage III: chemoradiation. Stage IV: systemic therapy (targeted therapy if EGFR/ALK/ROS1/Pd-L1 positive; immunotherapy; chemo). SCLC: limited → chemoradiation; extensive → chemo + immunotherapy. Palliative care. Smoking cessation.

stacks.label: Biopsy (bronchoscopic / CT-guided / surgical)
stacks.finding: Tissue diagnosis. NSCLC vs SCLC. Molecular testing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, PD-L1).
